request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Patient Information: 
Name: Not specified
Age: 62
Gender: Male

Hospital Course: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain and distension for the past month, which worsened in the last five days. The patient was diagnosed with small intestinal obstruction and underwent emergency laparotomy. During the operation, a small amount of food fiber was expelled, and multiple “stenosis rings” were found in the intestinal lumen at approximately 40 cm from the distal obstruction. The diseased bowel was removed, and the patient recovered without any discomfort. Pathological findings reported intestinal stenosis, mucosal erosion, and inflammatory granulation tissue formation. It showed neutrophil infiltration and vasodilation and congestion in the serosa. The muscle layer and serosa layer did not show any structural abnormality.

Summary of Hospital Stay: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain and distension for the past month and was diagnosed with small intestinal obstruction. The patient underwent emergency laparotomy, and a diseased bowel was removed. The pathological findings reported intestinal stenosis and mucosal erosion. The patient recovered well without any discomfort. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Condition at Discharge: 
Recovered.

Follow-up Plan: 
Patient was followed up for two months, and no discomfort was found. No further treatment is required at this time.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
This presentation points to multiple "diaphragm-like" stenosis rings in the small bowel, with mucosal erosion and nonspecific inflammatory granulation tissue and no muscle or serosal abnormality. That pattern is typical of NSAID-induced diaphragm disease of the small intestine. Eosinophils are not mentioned, and the findings are nonspecific.

The candidate codes are:
- K56 (paralytic ileus and intestinal obstruction without hernia). K56.6 is other and unspecified intestinal obstruction, and K56.5 is adhesions.
- K63.1 (perforation) and K63.8 (other specified diseases of intestine). Stricture of the intestine is K56.6 in ICD-10 and K63.8 in some contexts.
- K31.5 (obstruction of duodenum), which does not apply.
- K55 (vascular disorders of intestine), which does not apply.
- K50 (Crohn's disease), which is not supported by the findings.

The diagnosis was likely "small intestinal obstruction due to diaphragm disease" or "ulcerative stenosis." The pathology shows mucosal erosion with inflammatory granulation tissue, which could suggest nonspecific multiple ulcers of the small intestine (chronic enteropathy associated with SLCO2A1, or CEAS). ICD-10 has K63.3 (ulcer of intestine), but the obstruction is the reason for the operation and the principal diagnosis. In ICD-10, stricture of the intestine is indexed to K56.6 (ICD-10-AM: K56.6 other and unspecified intestinal obstruction). Because the stenosis is the main condition and the obstruction is what was treated, K56 is the best choice.

CODE: K56
